transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I’m just... exhausted. But in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. Which is frustrating because I actually just bought a brand new mattress last month. It’s one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box? My sister swore by it. She lives out in Denver now and she’s always hiking and doing all these outdoorsy things, so I figured if it helps her, it should be great for me, right? Though getting that box up the stairs was an absolute nightmare. The delivery guy just left it at the bottom of the porch and didn't even ring the bell. 

But anyway, yeah, the new bed isn't helping. Just getting through a normal workday—and I manage a team of twelve, so there's literally always some sort of interpersonal drama going on in the office—and then trying to get through dinner at home... it all just feels so much heavier than it should right now. I don't know why it's so hard to just do my normal routine.
Can you tell me more about this exhaustion you're feeling? For how long have you been feeling this way, and does it feel worse than usual fatigue you've experienced before?

It’s definitely way worse than normal fatigue. It’s just this... persistently low feeling. And it's been going on for about a month now. Which is honestly so jarring, because right before this recent swing, I was the exact opposite—unusually energized and driven. Like, I had so much energy I actually repainted my entire home office by myself in a single weekend. 

I picked out this color called "Sea Salt" because the guy at the hardware store—Gary, I think his name was—said it was a calming, neutral grey. But Gary was completely wrong, because in the afternoon light it just looks like mint toothpaste. I spent like three hours looking at those little paper swatches, too. Have you ever noticed how the lighting in those stores completely distorts everything? It’s those huge fluorescent bulbs. They are so harsh. My office building uses the exact same ones, and I’ve been trying to get building maintenance to swap them out for warm LEDs for over a year, but they just ignore my emails. It’s like talking to a brick wall with those people. And don't even get me started on the thermostat in that building. Half my team is wearing winter coats at their desks in July... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. Just... really, really tired.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling like activities that used to be pleasurable now feel flat or uninteresting?

Yeah, I have. Normally, I absolutely love painting, and I’m always wandering through museum exhibits on the weekends. But lately... I don't know, my painting supplies are just sitting there completely untouched. 

Which is a real shame, honestly, because I just bought these gorgeous, incredibly expensive sable brushes from this little independent art store downtown. Have you ever tried parking downtown lately? It is an absolute nightmare. They just raised the meter rates to something ridiculous, like four dollars an hour, and the spots are so narrow I can barely fit my car in them. Someone actually dinged my passenger door last month while I was grabbing coffee and didn't even leave a note. Who does that? Just drives away? I tried to fix the scratch with one of those buffing pens you see on late-night infomercials—you know, the ones where the guy is practically yelling at the camera about the magic of resin or whatever? It didn't work at all. It just made the clear coat look all cloudy and weird. I should probably take it to a body shop, but who has the time to deal with rental cars and insurance adjusters? 

But anyway... what was the question? Oh, right, things I enjoy. Yeah, even the museum... they have this new impressionist exhibit I've been looking forward to all year, but I just can't make myself care enough to actually go. It all just feels completely flat right now.
Has this feeling of flatness or lack of interest in things you used to enjoy been constant throughout the day, nearly every day, for the past month?

Yeah, pretty much. Most days lately, I just wake up with this... heavy, gray feeling. It's like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts, you know? Almost like waking up to a rainy Monday morning, except it's every single day. 

Speaking of rain, my gutters have been overflowing every time we get a decent storm lately. I think they're clogged with those little helicopter seeds from the maple tree in my neighbor's yard. I don't even know why he keeps that tree, honestly. The roots are completely destroying the sidewalk out front. I tripped over a raised piece of concrete just last week while I was walking my dog, Buster. He's a rescue—part beagle, part who-knows-what—and he has this terrible habit of pulling on the leash whenever he sees a squirrel. Anyway, I almost dropped my phone when I tripped. Thank goodness I had one of those heavy-duty cases on it. I bought it online after I dropped my last phone in the grocery store parking lot. The screen shattered into a million pieces, and the guy at the repair kiosk in the mall charged me way too much to fix it. He was wearing this incredibly strong cologne, too—like, overpowering pine scent. It gave me a headache for the rest of the afternoon. 

But yeah, anyway... that heavy feeling. It's just there all the time right now. Every day.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue, separate from the exhaustion you've already described, nearly every day for the past month?

Yeah, it's... it's just this constant, draining fatigue. It's exactly why I'm here, honestly. I'm just exhausted in a way that sleep doesn't even touch. Like, just getting through a normal workday and then coming home to make dinner feels so much heavier than it should. 

Speaking of dinner, I tried making this new slow-cooker pot roast recipe the other night. The recipe said it would be "fall-apart tender," but I swear it came out like a leather shoe. I think my crockpot is running too hot on the low setting. It's one of those older models with the floral pattern on the outside—my mother-in-law gave it to us years ago. She has this habit of giving us appliances she doesn't want anymore and calling them "heirlooms." Like, no, Barbara, a toaster oven from 1998 is not a family heirloom. It's just a fire hazard. We actually had a small grease fire in our kitchen a few years ago because of a faulty toaster. The smoke alarms went off, and it completely ruined the paint on the ceiling. We had to hire this guy, Dave, to come scrape the popcorn texture off and repaint it. Dave was a nice guy, but he talked constantly about his model train collection. Like, for hours. I know more about N-scale locomotives than I ever thought possible. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, the fatigue. Yeah, it's just... it's every single day. Just so heavy.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently, nearly every day for the past month?

Well, yeah, actually. I've been picking at my meals lately, or just completely forgetting to eat lunch at work. And my skirts are definitely fitting a little looser, even though I'm absolutely not trying to lose weight. 

Which is funny because normally, I'm the one organizing the office potlucks. I actually made this incredible spinach dip for our quarterly review meeting last month. I use water chestnuts in it for extra crunch, which is a secret my aunt taught me. She used to run this little catering business out of her basement back in the eighties. She made the best Swedish meatballs, too. But anyway, the dip was a huge hit, except with Kevin from accounting. Kevin is on this new paleo-keto-whatever diet, and he practically gave me a lecture by the water cooler about the inflammatory properties of mayonnaise. Honestly, Kevin is exhausting. He's always wearing those toe-shoes, too—you know the ones? They look like gorilla feet. He claims they're better for his posture, but he still slouches at his desk all day. I sit right across from him, so I have a perfect view of his terrible posture and his weird shoes. I asked HR if I could move my desk closer to the window, but they said the floor plan is "optimized for collaboration." Collaboration, right. It's just an excuse to cram us all into an open-plan nightmare where I can hear every time Kevin crunches on his raw almonds. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, my appetite. Yeah, I'm just not eating much at all, and my clothes are definitely getting baggy.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or worthless lately, like you're a failure or that you're letting people down, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Yeah, I really have. It's like this constant loop in my head. I keep replaying every missed family plan, every tense conversation with my husband... I just feel like I'm letting everyone down, you know? Like I'm failing as a wife, a mother, and even as a manager at work. 

Speaking of work, my team is supposed to be launching this new software update next week, and the whole thing has been a complete disaster. Our lead developer, Greg, decided to take a spontaneous two-week vacation to Costa Rica right in the middle of the final testing phase. Costa Rica! He sent us a picture of himself zip-lining through the rainforest while we were all stuck in a conference room trying to figure out why the code kept crashing. I mean, who does that? And the worst part is, he didn't even leave clear documentation for the junior devs to follow. I spent three hours on Tuesday just trying to decipher his notes, which were basically just a bunch of sticky notes stuck to his monitor. One of them just said "Fix the thing" with a frowny face. What thing, Greg?! 

My husband told me I should just let it go and let his manager deal with it, but my husband doesn't really understand how office politics work. He's a freelance graphic designer, so he just works in his sweatpants all day and listens to true crime podcasts. He's been obsessed with this one podcast about a guy who faked his own death by pretending to fall off a cruise ship. It's actually kind of fascinating—the guy apparently hid out in a motel in Florida for three years before someone recognized him at a Denny's. Can you imagine? Just giving up your whole life to eat Moons Over My Hammy in hiding?

But um... sorry, what was the question? Oh, the guilt. Yeah, it's just really overwhelming right now. I just feel like a failure all around.
Have you noticed any problems with your concentration lately—like difficulty focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly—nearly every day for the past month?

Yeah, definitely. It's been really frustrating. Like, at work, I'll sit there with a simple staffing email open, and I just reread it over and over again because I can't decide what to say or which option makes sense. It's like my brain just stalls out. 

Speaking of emails, the new email client IT forced us to switch to last week is an absolute nightmare. They promised it would "streamline our communication," but the interface is so clunky, and the search function doesn't even work. I was trying to find an invoice from a vendor we used last year—this local bakery that did the cupcakes for our company anniversary. They made these amazing red velvet ones with actual cream cheese frosting, none of that artificial stuff. The owner, Brenda, is a sweetheart, but she's so old-school she still prefers faxing over email. Who even uses a fax machine anymore? I had to explain to our new intern, Chloe, what a fax tone sounds like. Chloe is nice, but she's constantly on TikTok during her lunch break, doing those little dances in the breakroom. It's so distracting when you're just trying to microwave your soup. Last week she accidentally knocked over someone's Tupperware while trying to film a transition video. It was Carol's leftover lasagna, and Carol was furious. You do not mess with Carol's lunch. She's been with the company for twenty years and still uses a Rolodex. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my focus. Yeah, it's just really bad. I can't seem to make even simple decisions lately.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about problems with concentration, focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly, which directly maps to Diminished Thinking.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. It's been really frustrating. Like, at work, I'll sit there with a simple staffing email open, and I just reread it over and over again because I can't decide what to say or which option makes sense. It's like my brain just stalls out. 

Speaking of emails, the new email client IT forced us to switch to last week is an absolute nightmare. They promised it would "streamline our communication," but the interface is so clunky, and the search function doesn't even work. I was trying to find an invoice from a vendor we used last year—this local bakery that did the cupcakes for our company anniversary. They made these amazing red velvet ones with actual cream cheese frosting, none of that artificial stuff. The owner, Brenda, is a sweetheart, but she's so old-school she still prefers faxing over email. Who even uses a fax machine anymore? I had to explain to our new intern, Chloe, what a fax tone sounds like. Chloe is nice, but she's constantly on TikTok during her lunch break, doing those little dances in the breakroom. It's so distracting when you're just trying to microwave your soup. Last week she accidentally knocked over someone's Tupperware while trying to film a transition video. It was Carol's leftover lasagna, and Carol was furious. You do not mess with Carol's lunch. She's been with the company for twenty years and still uses a Rolodex. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my focus. Yeah, it's just really bad. I can't seem to make even simple decisions lately.

inference.note: The patient has endorsed symptoms consistent with a major depressive episode, including persistent depressed mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, fatigue, decreased appetite, feelings of guilt and worthlessness, and impaired concentration nearly every day for the past month. These symptoms appear to represent a continuation of the same illness process rather than a new episode, supporting the diagnosis of Recurrent Major Depressive Disorder, Current Episode Severe Without Psychotic Features (F33.3). No features of bipolar disorder or psychotic symptoms were endorsed, ruling out other candidates like F31.3 or F2x.x codes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a major depressive episode that meets criteria for recurrent severe depression without psychotic features. She describes persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, significant fatigue, decreased appetite with weight loss, feelings of guilt and worthlessness, and impaired concentration. These symptoms have been present nearly every day for the past month, and represent a significant decline from her prior functioning. Prior to this episode, she described a period of unusually high energy consistent with a hypomanic episode, supporting the diagnosis of a recurrent mood disorder rather than a single episode.
